title: kissed portuguese eggs frittata
description: jammy, chewy, energizing dish featuring sake-cooking and egg-free-friendly alternatives, perfect for breakfast or brunch
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the chickpea flour and vegetable oil until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the almond milk and sake.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and stir until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in the batter and let it cook for 2-3 minutes, until the edges start to set.
Distribute the diced tomatoes evenly over the batter, then use a spatula to gently lift and fold the edges of the frittata towards the center, allowing the uncooked batter to flow to the edges.
Return the skillet to the heat and cook for another 2-3 minutes, until the edges are set and the center is still slightly jiggly.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes, until the frittata is puffed and lightly golden.
Remove the skillet from the oven and garnish with chopped parsley, salt, and pepper to taste.
Let the frittata cool for a few minutes before slicing it into wedges and serving.
Serve warm or at room temperature, either on its own or with your favorite sides or toppings.
Experiment with different flavor combinations by adding various herbs, spices, or other ingredients to the frittata batter or toppings.
Storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
